metadata.title: Predicting adolescents’ environmental action: From individual to national-level factors using an explainable machine learning approach

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study uses the PISA 2018 dataset and reports that PISA employs a two-stage stratified probability-proportional-to-size design with response-rate targets at the school and student levels, and that non-qualifying systems are excluded from the public database. In the provided methods, the authors do not state that they applied PISA sampling weights (e.g., W_FSTUWT/TOTWGT) or any replicate-weight scheme during model training or evaluation. Because the analysis is based on standard ML classifiers (LightGBM, XGBoost, Random Forest, MLP) and the manuscript does not describe weight-aware training, the extraction treats the models as unweighted. The analytic sample is restricted to adolescents who answered the environmental-action items, and the dataset is further preprocessed via MICE-based predictive mean matching imputation and SMOTE oversampling before training/testing.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: Plausible values are not applicable because the dependent variables are private- and public-sphere environmental action indicators derived from PISA 2018 questionnaire items (classification targets), not cognitive achievement scores with PVs. Missing data handling is explicitly described: the authors impute missing values using predictive mean matching in the MICE package, which corresponds to multiple imputation. Therefore, PV handling is not part of the reported pipeline, while missingness is addressed through MICE before model training.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used the PISA 2018 dataset and restricted the analytic sample to adolescents who answered the environmental-action items; after excluding adolescents who did not answer these items, the final sample comprised 420,339 adolescents from 66 countries. No additional grade-level or school-type restrictions are reported in the provided text.

main_findings.dataset_used: PISA 2018 (15-year-olds) — environmental action items (public-sphere vs private-sphere)
main_findings.performance_metrics: LightGBM (validation): Accuracy 0.699, F1 0.698, Recall 0.699, AUC 0.762. LightGBM (test): Accuracy 0.700, F1 0.702, Recall 0.702, AUC 0.767.
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2018 the study leveraged environmental attitudes, international event discussion, mean Sustainable Development Score (SDS), ND-GAIN vulnerability, and school belonging to predict public-sphere environmental action, finding that LightGBM achieved the highest accuracy and AUC on both validation and test sets (test AUC = 0.767). This indicates that strengthening school-based civic/sustainability engagement and aligning it with supportive national sustainability contexts may improve adolescents’ likelihood of collective environmental participation, though the cross-sectional design limits causal claims.

main_findings.dataset_used: PISA 2018 (15-year-olds) — environmental action items (public-sphere vs private-sphere)
main_findings.performance_metrics: XGBoost (validation): Accuracy 0.830, Recall 0.830, AUC 0.709. XGBoost (test): Accuracy 0.833, Recall 0.833, AUC 0.718. Random Forest had the highest F1 (validation F1 0.780; test F1 0.781) while LightGBM had slightly lower F1 (test F1 0.772).
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2018 the study leveraged environmental attitudes, critical thinking, climate-change explanatory capacity, school collaboration atmosphere, and local climate-risk index to predict private-sphere environmental action, finding that XGBoost delivered the best accuracy/recall with strong generalization (test accuracy = 0.833, test AUC = 0.718). This indicates that interventions targeting individual competencies (e.g., climate understanding and critical thinking) together with supportive school climates may be particularly effective for promoting household/personal environmental behaviors, while unobserved contextual factors may still limit performance for public actions.

data.outcome_summary: The study uses PISA 2018 (66 countries; final analytic sample 420,339 adolescents after excluding non-responders to the environmental-action items) to predict two binary targets: private-sphere and public-sphere environmental actions. Four ML algorithms were trained with a 90/10 train-test split and stratified 10-fold cross-validation on the training set, with Optuna hyperparameter tuning; missing values were imputed using MICE predictive mean matching, and class imbalance was addressed via SMOTE. For public-sphere actions, LightGBM was best, reaching test Accuracy = 0.700, F1 = 0.702, Recall = 0.702, and AUC = 0.767. For private-sphere actions, XGBoost achieved the highest accuracy/recall (test Accuracy = 0.833, Recall = 0.833, AUC = 0.718), while Random Forest slightly led F1. The models use SHAP for interpretability, but SHAP-based feature importance is not causal, and the manuscript does not report applying PISA sampling weights in the ML pipeline.
